meta.title: Ruler AR: AI Tape Measure & Room Scanner for iPhone
meta.description: Use your iPhone as a tape measure. Point the camera to get length, area and angles, or scan a room into a floor plan. Free to download on the App Store.
meta.ogAlt: Ruler AR, iPhone tape measure app powered by LiDAR and ARKit
meta.keywords: tape measure app, AR ruler, iPhone measure app, LiDAR room scanner, AR tape measure, measuring app, floor plan app, distance measurement app

features.title: What you can do with it
features.intro: Hang a shelf, check whether a sofa will fit, work out how much flooring to buy. Most of that takes a few taps.

cameraMeasure.title: Point, tap, read the length
cameraMeasure.subtitle: Length and distance
cameraMeasure.body: Aim your iPhone at something and tap where it starts and ends. You get the length in centimetres, metres, inches or feet. It works best in good light, within about 5 metres.

lidarRoom.title: Scan a room with LiDAR
lidarRoom.subtitle: iPhone 12 Pro and newer Pro models
lidarRoom.body: Walk slowly around the room and the app draws walls, doors, windows and furniture as you go. Send the plan as a PDF or a 3D model to whoever needs it. You need a Pro iPhone or iPad with LiDAR.

manualRoom.title: No LiDAR? Draw the room as you walk
manualRoom.subtitle: Floor plans without LiDAR
manualRoom.body: Walk along each wall and tap the corners. The app straightens the lines, warns you if walls cross, and shows a small map as you go.

angleSquare.title: Check angles and corners
angleSquare.subtitle: AR protractor
angleSquare.body: Measure the angle between two surfaces to see whether a corner is really square. Handy for cabinets, shelves and picture frames.

bubbleLevel.title: A spirit level in your pocket
bubbleLevel.subtitle: Bubble level
bubbleLevel.body: Use the phone's sensors to level a shelf, a frame or a washing machine, or to find out which way the floor slopes.

export.title: Keep it and send it
export.subtitle: History, folders, PDF
export.body: Measurements go into your history, and you can sort them into project folders with notes and photos. Send a floor plan to a client as a PDF, or a single measurement by Messages or AirDrop.

useCases.title: Who it's useful for
useCases.intro: People who measure for work, and people who just want to know whether the bookshelf fits.

contractors.title: Contractors & remodelers
contractors.body: Site visits and change orders. Send a PDF of the measurements and floor plan before you leave the job.

designers.title: Interior designers
designers.body: Scan a room on the first visit and share the plan with your client.

diy.title: DIY & home renovation
diy.body: Measure for paint, tile, flooring and wallpaper. The material calculator turns the numbers into a shopping list.

realEstate.title: Real estate agents
realEstate.body: Make a floor plan during the walkthrough. Buyers see measurements, not a guess.

furniture.title: Furniture shopping
furniture.body: Will the couch fit? Measure the space, save it, and check it in the store.

everyday.title: Everyday measurements
everyday.body: A package, a parking spot, a kid's height. When the tape measure is in the garage, your iPhone is in your pocket.

compare.title: Tape measure app vs. the alternatives
compare.intro: There are three ways to measure a room. Here's how they compare.
compare.footnote: Checked for app version 5.3. In Ruler AR, room scans, height and plan export may need a subscription. iPhone Measure is Apple's built-in Measure app.

open.title: Open & aim
open.body: Open the app and point your iPhone at the wall, floor or object you want to measure.

point.title: Tap start and end
point.body: Tap where it starts, move the phone to where it ends, and tap again. The length appears on screen in cm, m, inches or feet.

export.title: Save, share, export
export.body: Every measurement goes into your history. Send a PDF to a client, share a screenshot, or keep it for later.

items.q: Does Ruler AR require a LiDAR sensor?
items.a: No. Length, area, angles, the bubble level and the manual room builder all work without it. You only need LiDAR for the automatic 3D room scan (iPhone 12 Pro and newer Pro models, iPad Pro 2020 and later).

items.q: How accurate is the AR tape measure?
items.a: Usually within a couple of centimetres indoors, in good light, up to about 5 metres. iPhones with LiDAR tend to do better. Touch Mode measures from the phone itself, which helps on short distances. If you're about to cut something expensive, check it with a real tape.

items.q: Can I export measurements to PDF?
items.a: Yes. Saved room plans can be exported as a PDF with the floor plan and a table of dimensions, then sent by Mail, Messages or AirDrop. Plan export may need a subscription.

It's free to download, and length, area, angles and the bubble level work without paying. The free version shows ads. Room scans, height and plan export may need a subscription, and you'll see the price in the app before you pay.

items.q: Which iPhones and iPads are supported?
items.a: Any device running iOS 16.6 or later. The app is optimised for the iPhone Xs through iPhone 17 Pro, iPad Pro (2018+), and iPad Air (2020+). On older non-LiDAR devices the app automatically switches to the Manual Room Builder.

items.q: How do I measure a room with my iPhone?
items.a: If your iPhone has LiDAR (12 Pro and newer): open Room Plan, walk slowly around the room, the app builds a 3D floor plan as you go. If no LiDAR: open Manual Room Builder, stand in a corner, walk along each wall tapping corners, the app generates a clean orthogonal floor plan.

items.q: Does it work in low light?
items.a: Yes, but it's less accurate. In dim rooms the app suggests turning on the flashlight with one tap. More light always helps.

Yes. The app runs on iPad Pro (2018+), iPad Air (2020+), and iPad mini (6th gen+), anything with iOS/iPadOS 16.6 or newer. iPad Pro models with LiDAR support the full 3D RoomPlan scanner. Larger iPad screens are particularly useful for the manual floor plan editor.

Yes, but accuracy depends on lighting. In open shade or overcast, AR tracking works as well as indoors. In direct sunlight, LiDAR depth readings can be washed out by the sun's IR, measurements still work but tolerance widens to a few cm at distance. For long outdoor runs (over 5 m), a laser distance meter is more reliable.

items.q: Will it work on iPhone 16 and 17?
items.a: Yes. It runs on iPhone 16 and 17 models. Models with LiDAR also get the automatic 3D room scan.
Not currently. The app is built on Apple's ARKit and RoomPlan frameworks, which have no direct Android equivalent. We're tracking ARCore developments but have no release timeline for Android.

items.q: Does the app collect tracking data?
items.a: The free version shows ads, which can use identifiers if you allow tracking when iOS asks. Ruler Pro has no ads. Details are in the App Store privacy label and our privacy policy.
